phase: 4p (frame allocation order made once per loaded catalog)
profile_before: phone DWARF profile rtr1b-dwarf: OriginalContactFrameMemory.init 4.5% of the main thread (its sort comparator): world contacts and actor hits each build the contact frame memory every gameplay tick, sorting the indices of ~14,600 frame allocations by address

rejected_first_version.what: skip the sort when the allocations are already in strictly increasing address order (one pass)
rejected_first_version.result: main 23.4/23.4 ms (within variation); a DWARF profile (rt4p-dwarf) showed OriginalContactFrameMemory.init at 6.0%: the allocations are not in increasing address order, so the sort still ran plus the extra pass; stopped before its suites finished and not committed

change: OriginalLoadedCatalog keeps frameAllocationOrder (the indices of frameAllocations sorted by address with the same comparator, made once at load); OriginalContactFrameMemory gains init(_:order:) (a count precondition); world contacts and actor hits pass state.catalog.frameAllocationOrder. A match's frame allocations are the catalog's with the same addresses in the same order (addresses are let; only actor hits write them back, after storage writes); the sorting init stays for callers with arbitrary allocations

phone.result: main 23.6/23.3 -> 21.8/21.9 ms per tick, complete 18.4 -> 16.5 ms (more than the profile's share suggested)
phone.note: the rows keep the fields recorded in the session; their remaining fields (run seconds, peak memory, ticks per second, busy seconds) were only in the jobs' terminal output, which the Mac's restart at about 12:50 deleted with the scratchpad

gates.scenarios: all 10 equal (counted before the restart); frames identical, recompared after it (rt-4p2-all: 1,832 frames)
gates.AppKit: vs and playback equal; 3,960 frames identical to the R1 AppKit run (recompared after the restart)
gates.emulator: vs equal, 1,832 frames identical (before the restart)
gates.tests: bundle B (native tree 99428728, the same as this commit's): all 173 suites (the 172 plus OriginalContactFrameMemoryTests), 504 tests, pass: 134 before the restart, the interrupted one and the 38 not yet run rerun on the same bundle after it (logs rt4p2-* and rt4p2r-*)

review: independent read-only review: approve; the invariant holds (addresses let, catalog let, two production assignments of frameAllocations, neither reorders; read(_:retaining:) keeps catalog and frames together; nothing appends or reorders during a match); the precomputed order is the same permutation (same comparator; production addresses are unique, OriginalFrameHeap rejects overlaps); each construction site uses the right init; ~114 KiB per catalog, shared by copies. Not applied (optional): a debug-only sortedness assertion, a write test, a real-catalog invariant check.
